predictions.selection_reason: User-controlled path without root -> resolve() -> ensures absolute path resolution for security
predictions.source_summary: this.path comes from SendStream constructor parameter, which is typically user-controlled request path
predictions.sink_summary: fs.stat(path) and this.send(path, stat) for file system operations
predictions.guard_summary: Null byte check, '..' path traversal check via upPathRegexp, dotfile handling with _hidden option, root directory confinement when root is set
predictions.risk_pattern: User-controlled path resolved to absolute path without root confinement, then used in file system operations

unresolved_facts: Exact behavior of upPathRegexp pattern matching
Whether path.resolve provides any security benefits over normalization alone

top_sast_rules.cwe_name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')
top_sast_rules.description: Extracting files from a malicious ZIP file, or similar type of archive, without validating that the destination file path is within the destination directory can allow an attacker to unexpectedly gain access to resources.
top_sast_rules.pattern: Look for security-sensitive operations that handle user input without proper validation or sanitization
top_sast_rules.remediation: Implement path validation using canonical paths. Reject paths containing '../' or similar traversal sequences.

top_sast_rules.cwe_name: Improper Link Resolution Before File Access ('Link Following')
top_sast_rules.description: File access follows a symlink, hardlink, or shortcut to an unintended resource.
